To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The Spanish press is characterized by a high degree of polarization in its opinion articles; (2) the opinion articles are characterized by a high percentage of negative opinions about the political parties and politicians; (3) the political parties and the politicians have a high percentage of positive opinions about themselves; and (4) the opinion articles in the press have a high percentage in their content of the topics related to the electoral campaign.

the Spanish newspapers have published more articles in the period of the General Elections than in other periods, and that the articles have been written by opinion makers from the political parties, the trade unions and the business associations, and that the topics that have received more articles are the political leaders and their speeches.

the analysis of the articles of opinion published in the Spanish written press during the General Elections campaign of 2015 has allowed us to identify the actors that have participated as opinion leaders, the topics that were treated, the form and the context in which they have been presented, and, in sum the scenario proposed by written press opinion in the public political debate.

the opinion in the Spanish press has been dominated by the two main political parties: PSOE and PP, and by the two main opinion makers of the political spectrum: Jose Ignacio Torreblanca and Ignacio Escolar.
